Taqwim user manual

On this page
  • Chapters
  • How to read this manual
  • What works where

Welcome to Taqwim (تقويم), a free app for prayer times, the Hijri and other calendars, the Qibla and astronomy. Taqwim has no ads, no accounts and no tracking, and it does its calculations on your device, so almost everything works without an internet connection.

Taqwim runs on Android, iPhone and iPad, Windows, macOS, Linux and in a web browser. The screens are the same everywhere; where a feature depends on the device, this manual says so.

Chapters

  1. Getting started: installing Taqwim, the first launch, choosing your location and finding your way around.
  2. Prayer times: the day's times, the countdown, the calculation methods and adjustments.
  3. Alerts and the Athan: prayer alerts, reminders, the built-in Athan and your own sounds.
  4. Calendar and Islamic occasions: the calendar screen, the Hijri calendar choices, the date converter, the age calculator and the occasions of the year.
  5. The Qibla: the Qibla locator, the Sun method, and the 2-D and 3-D compasses.
  6. Maps, nearby mosques and offline areas: the Qibla map, mosques near you, directions and guidance, and maps you can use offline.
  7. Sky, Moon and astronomy: the Sun, day and night, the Moon and the new crescent, eclipses, the planets, magnetism and the 3-D sky sphere.
  8. The Astronomical Calculator: year cycles, the Moon at any moment, and prayer times for a day in history.
  9. Settings: every setting and its default.
  10. Backup and restore: keeping your settings safe and moving them to a new device.
  11. Troubleshooting and questions: late or silent alerts, location problems, a Hijri date one day off, and more.
  12. Privacy and credits: what stays on your device, and who made the data Taqwim uses.

How to read this manual

  • Names of buttons, tabs and settings are written in bold, exactly as the English interface shows them. The Arabic manual uses the Arabic labels.
  • "Tap" also means "click" on a computer.
  • Steps that change something are numbered; read them in order.

Taqwim is used in many countries with different customs. Where the app offers a choice (the calculation method, the Asr time, the Hijri calendar), follow your local authority or mosque. The app explains each choice but does not decide for you.

What works where

Most of Taqwim is the same on every device. These features depend on the device:

FeatureWhere it works
Prayer alerts and the AthanAndroid, iPhone and iPad. Not yet on Windows, macOS, Linux or the web.
The built-in Athan sounds and your own soundsEvery app except the web version.
Nearby mosques, directions and offline map areasEvery app except the web version.
Spoken guidance to a mosqueAndroid, iPhone and iPad. Computers show the guidance without voice.
A live compass (Qibla dial, 3-D compass, live sky)Devices with a compass sensor, such as most phones and tablets. On a computer you turn the view by hand.
Backup fileEvery version. The web version's backup holds the settings but not sounds.
